attributes.body_ja:
「訳（わけ）」は、「原因（げんいん）」「理由（りゆう）」「意味（いみ）」「結論（けつろん）」など、いろいろな意味（いみ）を持（も）つ言葉（ことば）です。

意味（いみ）はいろいろありますが、どのような場合（ばあい）も、「わけ」は、物事（ものごと）を強（つよ）く判断（はんだん）したり結論（けつろん）付（づ）けたりするときに使（つか）われます。この「わけ」を使（つか）った最（もっと）も基本的（きほんてき）な文法（ぶんぽう）は「わけだ」です。これは「わけ」と助動詞（じょどうし）「だ」からできています。

「わけだ」は、文（ぶん）の終（お）わりで使（つか）われます。そして、「(A) だから (B) なのだ」や「(A) だから、当然（とうぜん） (B) だ」などの意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。また、「という」が「わけだ」の前（まえ）に付（つ）くこともあります。

「わけ」は名詞（めいし）なので、その前（まえ）には連体形（れんたいけい）の語（ご）が置（お）かれます。また、「わけ」はただ理由（りゆう）を示（しめ）すだけでなく「なるほど」「やっぱり」「当然（とうぜん）」のように、納得（なっとく）のニュアンスや、理由（りゆう）を強調（きょうちょう）するニュアンスを出（だ）すこともできます。

「わけ」は、話（はな）し手（て）が聞（き）いた内容（ないよう）を確（たし）かめたいときに、疑問（ぎもん）の形（かたち）で使（つか）われることもあります。このときは、「わけだね」や「わけですか」のような言（い）い方（かた）をします。
attributes.body:
One of the most misunderstood words in Japanese is 訳（わけ）. Of the many ways it can be translated, the most common are 'reason', 'cause', 'meaning', or 'conclusion'. Despite this, it may be beneficial to consider it almost identical to an equally versatile English word 'so'.

In all of its uses, わけ simply highlights the plain existence/determination of something in the same way that 'so' does in English. This can be seen in its most basic form in わけだ. A combination of わけ and the auxiliary verb だ.

わけだ will be used at the end of sentences, and is sometimes preceded by という. This use is often translated as 'for the reason of (A)', 'no wonder its (A)', or 'its (A), as you'd expect'. Realistically though, it just means 'it is so that it's (A)', or 'so it's (A)'.

Due to わけ being a noun, it will need to follow the attributive form of whatever word comes before it. As we can see 'so' and わけ have an extremely close pattern of nuances, ranging from 'because', all the way through to simple emphasis (like with 'naturally', and 'as you'd expect').

わけ may also be used in questions, implying that the speaker is trying to determine something that they have heard. わけだね 'so its (A) right?', and わけですか 'so is it that (A)?' are good examples of this.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: はずがない denies something based on logic or evidence, while わけだ draws a conclusion or explains a reason. For example, 来るはずがない ('There's no way he'll come.') vs. 来るわけだ ('So that's why he's coming.'). One rejects a possibility, while the other clarifies it.

first_relatable.title: はずがない
first_relatable.meaning: Hardly possible, Cannot be, Highly unlikely, Improbable

second_relatable.title: わけだ
second_relatable.meaning: For that reason, No wonder, As you'd expect, Naturally, Thus, This is why

attributes.body: わけだ and ため(に) are similar in that both can be used when expressing a reason, but they mean quite different things. わけだ is used when drawing a conclusion, like the English 'so that's why (A)', while ため(に) on the other hand means 'for the sake of (A)' or 'due to (A)'.

first_relatable.title: わけだ
first_relatable.meaning: For that reason, No wonder, As you'd expect, Naturally, Thus, This is why

second_relatable.title: ため(に)
second_relatable.meaning: For, For the sake of, In order to

attributes.body: Both だけに and わけだ can be used to draw conclusions, but differ in tone and focus. だけに emphasizes an expected result based on a known condition, e.g. 忙しい人だけに来ないと思った ('Precisely because he's a busy man, I thought he wouldn't come'), while わけだ indicates the speaker's realization based on something previously expressed or observed, e.g. だから来ないわけだ ('So that's why he's not coming').

first_relatable.title: だけに
first_relatable.meaning: As might be expected, Because, All the more because, It's only natural

second_relatable.title: わけだ
second_relatable.meaning: For that reason, No wonder, As you'd expect, Naturally, Thus, This is why

attributes.body: Both だけのことはある and わけだ can be used when drawing conclusions, but function differently. だけのことはある affirms that an outcome is appropriate or deserved in a positive sense, e.g. プロだけのことはある ('It's as expected from a pro'), while わけだ signals the speaker's understanding or conclusion, e.g. だから負けたわけだ ('So that's why we lost'). The latter conveys realization, in either a positive or negative sense.

first_relatable.title: だけのことはある
first_relatable.meaning: No wonder, Not surprising that, As expected

second_relatable.title: わけだ
second_relatable.meaning: For that reason, No wonder, As you'd expect, Naturally, Thus, This is why

attributes.body: Both express reasoning in a broad sense, but are used differently. わけだ explains why something is the case, e.g. 暖房が壊れているのか。だから寒いわけだ ('So the heater's broken. That explains why it's cold.') ことだ gives strong advice or instruction, e.g. 寒いなら暖房をつけることだ ('If it's cold, you should turn on the heater.')

first_relatable.title: わけだ
first_relatable.meaning: For that reason, No wonder, As you'd expect, Naturally, Thus, This is why

attributes.body: Both express logical conclusions, but with different emphasis. はずだ conveys expectation or prediction, as in 来るはずだ ('He should come.'). わけだ explains a reason behind something known or observed, like 来るわけだ ('So that's why he's coming.'). はずだ leans future-oriented, わけだ explanatory.

first_relatable.title: わけだ
first_relatable.meaning: For that reason, No wonder, As you'd expect, Naturally, Thus, This is why

second_relatable.title: はずだ
second_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)
